en.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Official Price $1.50/$7.50 (Nov 12)
en.titleCore: Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Google's Model Card and Price, November 12, 2026
en.description: Google published a Gemini 4 Hydrogen model card on Nov 12, 2026, with $1.50 input and $7.50 output per million tokens listed. What is confirmed, and what is not.
en.body:
On November 12, 2026, Google published a model card for Gemini 4 Hydrogen (model ID gemini-4-hydrogen), and its Gemini API pricing page lists it at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens on the standard paid tier, with no dated price change. Unlike the Krypton rumours, this model has a vendor page and a price. Neither page says whether it is in preview.

What Google has published

  • Model card. Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 Hydrogen card is marked "Published 12 November 2026" and says the model is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. It positions Hydrogen as a faster model for everyday coding and agentic workflows, while Carbon and Argon are the frontier models. It lists a combined input and output context window of up to 1M tokens, up to 64K default synchronous output tokens, and up to 1M through background long decode.
  • Where it is offered. The card lists the Gemini app, Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Gemini for business, Google Antigravity, Google Sheets and Google Search.
  • Price. The Google AI Studio pricing page lists the standard paid tier at $1.50 input and $7.50 output per million tokens, output including thinking tokens, and $0.075 for cached input. The note says caching is implicit only; explicit caching is not supported. The page shows no future-dated change for Hydrogen and no preview label.

Price against the other Gemini 4 models

ModelInput per 1M, standardOutput per 1M, standardDated change
Gemini 4 Hydrogen$1.50$7.50None listed
Gemini 4 Carbon$2.00$10.00$4.00 and $20.00 from December 1, 2026
Gemini 4 Argon$2.00$10.00$4.00 and $20.00 from December 1, 2026

Against today's Carbon and Argon rates, Hydrogen is 25% cheaper per input and output token ($1.50 against $2.00, $7.50 against $10.00). Against the December 1 rates it is 62.5% cheaper ($1.50 against $4.00, $7.50 against $20.00). These are our calculations from the listed prices, not Google's. A lower token price is not a lower cost per task if a model needs more tokens to finish the work.

What the card says about quality

The card includes a benchmark table covering agentic coding, knowledge work, computer use, multimodal understanding, science and math, and reasoning, and compares Hydrogen with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Terra. Those are Google's own results. We have not reproduced them and do not quote scores here.

What this means for a budget

  1. Price it on the published rate, not the codename. Hydrogen has a model ID and a rate, so a forecast can carry it as a line item with its source date.
  2. Count thinking tokens. The pricing page lists output as including thinking tokens, so a model that reasons at length can cost more per task than its per-token price suggests.
  3. Test your own workload. A cost comparison needs your own prompts, token counts per task and the same grading criteria across Hydrogen, Carbon and Argon.

What we have not verified

  • Release status. The card and pricing page do not say whether Hydrogen is preview, general availability or limited access.
  • Benchmarks. All scores come from Google's card; we did not run them.
  • Batch, Flex and Priority rates, free-tier limits, the knowledge cutoff and any safety report. We did not check them.
  • Any link between Hydrogen and the Krypton tester posts. We found none.

All figures are as of November 12, 2026. Check the pricing page before you put a number in a finance document. For the models in the December 1 price step, see the Argon December 1 increase and Gemini 4 Carbon against Claude Fable 5.2.

faq.question: Is Gemini 4 Hydrogen available?
faq.answer: Google published a model card for it on November 12, 2026 and lists it on the Gemini API pricing page under the ID gemini-4-hydrogen. Neither page says whether it is in preview or generally available, so check AI Studio before relying on it.

faq.question: How much does Gemini 4 Hydrogen cost?
faq.answer: The Google AI Studio pricing page lists $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens on the standard paid tier, with thinking tokens included in output and $0.075 for cached input. No dated price change is listed.

faq.question: Is Gemini 4 Hydrogen the same as Krypton?
faq.answer: We found no evidence that it is. Krypton has been reported only through tester posts and Google has published nothing about it. Hydrogen has an official model card and a listed price.

faq.question: Are the Gemini 4 Hydrogen benchmarks independent?
faq.answer: No. The benchmark table is in Google's own model card, compared with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Terra. We have not reproduced the scores.
